title: Central Clearing and the CCP Loss Waterfall

maps.tested: Rated Moderately Important and described as largely a repeat of Part I, with one carve-out.
maps.specifics: The sheet's carve-out is explicit: 'know the loss waterfall.' Initial margin, default fund contribution of the defaulter, CCP equity tranche, mutualised default fund, assessments, in that order. Sequence errors are the distractor.

vardeezReading: CR-18: Moderate; "CCP is same as Level 1. Not likely to be testable. Just give a good read." with the note "Know Loss Waterfall".

selectors.name: Order of the CCP loss waterfall
selectors.what: The order in which a CCP's resources absorb a clearing member's default loss: (1) defaulter's initial margin; (2) defaulter's default fund contribution; (3) CCP skin-in-the-game (its own equity); (4) default fund of the non-defaulting members; (5) rights of assessment and/or other loss allocation; (6) remaining CCP capital; (7) liquidity support, or the CCP fails. Sequence errors, such as skin-in-the-game placed after the mutualised fund, pooling the defaulter's fund pro rata with survivors', or using survivors' initial margin (barred by EMIR 45(4)), are the distractors.

notSelected: CR-18 a, b, c, d and e (what a CCP is, novation, netting and compression, margin and default funds, CCP risk management), CR-18 g (methods beyond the default fund, such as assessments, VMGH, tear-up and forced allocation, apart from where they sit in the waterfall order), CR-18 h, i and j (bilateral versus central clearing, initial margin versus default fund, advantages and disadvantages) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
